question.text: Which of the following must a Regulated Entity ensure while adopting a Risk-Based Approach (RBA)?

answer.text: All three: the RBA is objective and proportionate to the risks; based on reasonable grounds; and reviewed and updated at appropriate intervals
The RBA is objective and proportionate to the risks
The RBA is based on reasonable grounds
The RBA is reviewed and updated at appropriate intervals

explanation.text: The Logic: The IFSCA Guidelines state that a Regulated Entity adopting an RBA shall ensure that: (i) the RBA is objective and proportionate to the risks; (ii) the RBA is based on reasonable grounds; and (iii) the RBA is reviewed and updated at appropriate intervals. All three conditions are mandatory and must be met together. The Trap: Each of the three single-condition distractors is individually correct as a statement, which makes them tempting. However, the question asks which set of conditions a Regulated Entity must ensure — the IFSCA Guidelines require all three to be satisfied, not just one. Note: Think of the RBA as a living framework: it must be objective, evidence-based, and refreshed periodically — none of the three conditions is optional.
